title: ClpC1-targeting peptide natural products differentially dysregulate the proteome of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
projectDescription: Targeting the protein quality control system in Mycobacterium tuberculosis offers a powerful and largely untapped opportunity for antibiotic development. The ClpC1:ClpP1P2 protease is an essential component of the system and is involved in both regulatory and stress-related protein degradation. Several non-ribosomal peptide natural product families have been discovered, including ecumicin, ilamycins (rufomycins) and cyclomarins, which bind to the ClpC1 chaperone and possess potent antimycobacterial activity. This has led to significant interest in these molecules, and the ClpC1:ClpP1P2 system more generally, as a bona fide target for the development of new tuberculosis drugs. In this study, we apply a systematic and multi-layered approach combining quantitative proteomics, bioinformatics, transcriptomics, CRISPRi gene knockdown, and targeted biochemical and biophysical assays to dissect the mechanisms of ecumicin, ilamycin and cyclomarin in clinically relevant Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Strikingly, despite exhibiting similar binding modes to ClpC1, each natural product elicits distinct substrate-specific effects on protein degradation. We further show that derivatives of ilamycin and ecumicin engage the stress-response chaperones ClpC2 and Hsp20 respectively with varied affinities. The differential disruption of ClpC1 substrates and stress-response chaperones, and distinct reshaping of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis proteome by the three natural products, unveils opportunities for the development of protein quality control-targeted antimycobacterials.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Mtb H37Rv treatment and cell lysis  Mtb H37Rv was grown until mid-log phase (OD600 ~ 0.5). For proteomics experiments Mtb was split into separate flasks containing 5 ml of bacteria and subsequently treated with each compound (MIC90) or vehicle control, DMSO. Flasks were incubated for 48 h at 37 ºC without agitation. For heat stress experiments, mid-log phase Mtb was treated with MIC90 of NPAs or DMSO and heat stress was induced with a 16 h incubation at 42 ºC whilst controls were incubated at 37 ºC for 16 h.  For proteomics experiments cells were pelleted by centrifugation at 3,750 g for 10 min. The supernatant was removed and pellets were resuspended in 200 µL of SDS lysis buffer (4%, 10 mM EDTA, 1x cOmplete protease inhibitor EDTA-free (Roche) in 1x phosphate buffered saline. Lysed cells were heated to 95 ºC in a water bath for 30 minutes to ensure complete sterilisation and were then frozen overnight (-20 ºC). Samples were thawed at 95ºC and sonicated for 10 minutes (30 s on, 30 s off) at 70% Amplitude. Lysates were clarified at 18,000 g for 10 min at room temp and protein concentration was determined by BCA total protein assay (Pierce).    Sample preparation for LC-MS/MS analysis  Lysates were thawed at 95 ºC and SDS was removed by chloroform/methanol protein precipitation. Briefly, for 100 µL of lysate; 400 µL methanol, 100 µL chloroform and 300 µL water was added to each sample. Samples were clarified at 9,000 g for 5 min at room temperature and the top 80% of the upper phase was aspirated. An additional 300 µL methanol was added, followed by clarification at 9,000 g for 5 min. The entire supernatant was aspirated and the pellet allowed to dry before resuspension in SDC buffer (4% sodium deoxycholate, 0.1M Tris-HCl, pH 8.0). Protein concentration was quantified by BCA total protein assay (Pierce). 20 µg of protein was reduced and alkylated with 10 mM TCEP, 40 mM chloroacetamide (CAA) for 10 min at 95 ºC. The SDC concentration was diluted to 1% with water and the samples were cooled to room temperature. Mtb lysates were digested with 200 ng trypsin and incubated for 16 h at 37 ºC with 1,000 rpm shaking in a Thermomixer-C (Eppendorf).   SDB-RPS peptide clean-up was performed prior to LC-MS/MS as described previously 64. An equal volume of 1% TFA in ethyl acetate was added to the digests and vortexed. SDB- RPS StageTips were constructed with 200 µL pipette tips packed with doubly stacked SDB- RPS discs (Sigma-Aldrich Cat No. 66886-U), punched with an 18-gauge needle. The StageTips were mounted into a custom 3D printed holder over a 96 well polypropylene waste plate. Each tip was wetted with 100 µL of acetonitrile, centrifuged at 1,000 g for 1 min and the flowthrough discarded. After wetting, tips were washed with 100 µL of 30% methanol, 1% TFA in H2O and centrifuged at 1,000 g for 3 min. Tips were equilibrated with 100 µL of 0.2% TFA in H2O and centrifuged for 3 min at 1,000 g. The bottom phase of the digests were loaded onto the tips and centrifuged for 5 min at 1,000 g. Loading was followed by two wash steps, both with 1% TFA in ethyl acetate with centrifugation for 3 min at 1000 g.  The last wash consisted of 100 µL of 0.2% TFA in H2O and centrifuged for 3 min at 1,000 g. The flow-through was discarded after each step. The waste plate was exchanged for a bottom plate containing a holder supporting an unskirted PCR plate. Peptides were eluted with 5% ammonium hydroxide and 15% H2O in acetonitrile and centrifuged for 5 min at 1000 g. The eluent was dried until <1 µL remained using nitrogen drying with a TurboVap 96 Dual (Biotage), with both plate and gas temperatures set to 65 ºC. The peptides were immediately resuspended with 20 µL of 5% (v/v) formic acid and the protein concentration was measured with a Direct Detect spectrometer (Millipore). Samples were stored at 4 ºC until ready to be analysed by LC-MS/MS.   LC-MS/MS analysis  Using a VanquishT Neo UHPLC system, Peptides in 5 % (v/v) formic acid were injected (3 µL) directly onto a 45 cm x 75 um C18 (Dr. Maisch, Ammerbuch, Germany, 1.9 µm) fused silica analytical column with a ~10 µm pulled tip, coupled to a nanospray ion source. Peptides were resolved over a gradient of 5% acetonitrile to 40 % acetonitrile over 90 min with a flow rate of 0.3 µL/ min. Peptides were ionized by electrospray ionization at 2.4 kV. Tandem mass spectrometry analysis was carried out on an Orbitrap ExplorisTM 480 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). MS1 spectra were generated in a 350-1650 m/z mass range at a 30 000 orbitrap resolution with a maximum injection time of 54 ms. Precursors were selected for MS2 analysis in a data independent acquisition (DIA) using 20 variable width isolation windows in the 350-1650 m/z mass range. HCD fragmentation was used with stepped collision energies of 25%, 27% and 30%. The orbitrap was operated at 30,000 resolution, with and AGC of 1x106 and a maximum injection time of 54 ms.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MSMS data and statistical analysis  Raw data was analysed in DIA-NN (version 1.8). The precursor false discovery rate was set to 1%, and the Mtb H37Rv UniProt database downloaded on 14th April 2022 was supplied for peptide identification that contained 4062 protein sequence entries. Library generation was enabled with charge states 1-4, precursor m/z from 350 to 1650.  Carbamidomethylation of Cys, N-terminal excision of Met and acetylation of protein N-termini were searched as fixed modification. Likely interreferences were removed and match between runs was enabled. Enzymatic specificity was set to trypsin with a maximum of 1 missed cleavage permitted.
